prompt:
Here is a problem from another field that shares the underlying structure of the research question below, with notes on how that field investigates it.

<parallel>
Field: Hydrology and catchment science
Problem: Whether a watershed's storage of water and sediment from earlier storms acts as a memory that determines how it responds to the next rainfall event, beyond what current rainfall predicts.
How it is studied: Hydrologists fit transfer-function or lagged-regression models that include antecedent wetness and check whether the residuals show persistent structure. They analyze hysteresis loops in rainfall-runoff or sediment-concentration plots, and they use paired-catchment experiments in which one basin is manipulated and its response is compared with an untreated control over many years.
</parallel>

Each of your ideas must transfer a specific method, measurement logic, or principle from how that field studies its problem, while still being a concrete, scientifically sound way to address the research question.

Research question: "What analyses or measurements would best test whether AP-1 acts as a cellular memory mechanism?"

Propose 5 distinct, concrete ideas (analyses, measurements, or experiments) that a research lab could pursue to address this question. For each idea give a short title and a description of one or two sentences.

ideas.title: Antecedent-state transfer-function model with residual diagnostics
ideas.description: Fit models that predict target-gene induction or enhancer activity from the current stimulus plus an exponentially weighted index of prior AP-1 activity, as hydrologists add antecedent wetness to rainfall-runoff models. If the antecedent term improves prediction and the residuals lose autocorrelation, that supports AP-1 carrying state forward beyond what the present stimulus explains.

ideas.title: Hysteresis loops of AP-1 activity versus stimulus dose
ideas.description: Ramp stimulus intensity up and then back down in single-cell time series (for example, Fos or c-Jun reporter intensity against stimulus level) and compare the rising and falling limbs as sediment-concentration hysteresis is compared. A loop that persists, with a nonzero enclosed area, means the cells' AP-1 output depends on their stimulation history rather than on the current dose alone.

ideas.title: Paired-lineage manipulation with long-term rechallenge
ideas.description: Split genetically matched cell populations into an AP-1-perturbed arm (for example, a degron-tagged or CRISPR-disrupted Jun/Fos) and an untreated control, then give repeated stimulation cycles over weeks and compare the second-response and later-response magnitudes. The difference in memory-like priming between arms, measured against the control over many cycles, isolates AP-1's contribution.

ideas.title: Recession analysis of AP-1 occupancy and chromatin persistence after washout
ideas.description: After removing the stimulus, track AP-1 binding (CUT&RUN or ChIP at time points) and chromatin accessibility (ATAC-seq) across hours to days, and fit exponential recession curves as hydrologists fit baseflow recession constants. Long decay constants at specific enhancers indicate stored AP-1 signal, and comparing these timescales with those of non-AP-1 transcription factors tests whether AP-1 specifically provides the storage.

ideas.title: Pulse-interval and antecedent-storage perturbation experiments
ideas.description: Deliver the same total AP-1 stimulation as pulses separated by different intervals, then measure re-induction after a standard challenge, and remove the putative storage (for example, by blocking AP-1 protein stability or chromatin retention) to see whether the memory effect disappears. Memory that depends on the interval and vanishes when storage is disrupted is direct evidence of an AP-1-based mechanism rather than a correlation with the current stimulus.
